what: A small screen on the wall that draws the shape of the sound you patch in, so you can see what the sound looks like. The sound itself passes through untouched.
how: The screen draws the wave as a line moving up and down with the sound: a smooth sine is a gentle hill, a saw is a ramp, a pulse is a box. It waits for the wave to cross zero going up, so a steady note stands still on the screen. Patch it in the middle of a chain to check what a module did, or just on a side branch. It changes nothing you hear.

ins.in: The signal to draw and pass on. Audio (-1..1) or a control signal; the screen shows -1 to 1.

outs.out: An exact copy of the input. Patch it onward (to a filter, OUT or whatever comes next), or leave it empty and use the scope as a side branch.

knobs.time: How much time fits across the screen, from 1 to 100 milliseconds. Small shows one wave stretched out; large squeezes in many waves. A low note needs a bigger value to see a whole cycle.
knobs.gain: Makes the drawing taller or shorter, from a quarter to four times. Only the picture changes, not the sound.

try: Patch VCO's out into SCOPE's in and SCOPE's out into OUT's left. Play a note, turn the VCO's WAVE through its shapes and watch each one on the screen. Raise TIME if you see only a blur.
